Question: Who handles complaints independently after a provider response, when can a complaint be made or escalated, what are the stages and response times, and how does someone apply?
After a provider response, the complaint can be handled by HDC’s Complaints Assessment Team and, if needed, a formal investigation; if a breach is found after formal investigation, the case may very rarely be referred to the Director of Proceedings. A complaint can be made to HDC after trying to talk or write to the provider first, and if issues persist or that is not suitable; the page says complaints can also be escalated if a provider does not respond timely and appropriately. The stages are: submit your complaint, assessment, possible provider/advocacy resolution, referral to another agency, closure, or formal investigation; response times are an update about every three months, a decision can take from a few days to a year or more, and a formal investigation often takes about two years.
